sections.content: En definitiva (ultimately, in short) signals that a sentence is drawing together several previous points into one final conclusion -- a useful way to close a comparison after listing multiple examples or differences. It's a common closing move in synthesis writing. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: En definitiva, ningún régimen militar de la región logró sostenerse de manera indefinida.
items.english: Ultimately, no military regime in the region managed to sustain itself indefinitely.

items.spanish: Cada régimen tomó un camino distinto, pero, en definitiva, todos se enfrentaron a los mismos tipos de presión.
items.english: Each regime took a different path, but ultimately, all of them faced the same kinds of pressure.

items.spanish: En definitiva, la combinación de crisis económica y pérdida de legitimidad resultó, tarde o temprano, decisiva en cada caso.
items.english: In the end, the combination of economic crisis and loss of legitimacy proved decisive, sooner or later, in every case.

items.spanish: En definitiva, comparar estos tres países muestra tanto lo que compartían como lo profundamente distintos que fueron sus finales.
items.english: Ultimately, comparing these three countries shows both what they shared and how profoundly different their endings were.

sections.content: En definitiva works best at the start of a concluding sentence, after several supporting points have already been given -- it signals I'm about to sum this all up, unlike en definitiva's near-synonym al fin y al cabo, which leans more toward after all (justifying rather than concluding).
